questions.stem: What was one of the biggest criticisms of early data lakes that Delta Lake set out to solve?
options: They could not store unstructured data
Their lack of reliability, with no transactional integrity or data consistency on file-based storage
They were too small to hold enterprise data
They could not be queried with Spark
questions.explanation: Early lakes excelled at storing vast volumes of data but struggled to provide the transactional integrity and consistency that databases and warehouses delivered as a matter of course.

questions.stem: What does DML (Data Manipulation Language) refer to?
options: Operations such as inserts, updates and deletes
The metadata catalogue of a data lake
questions.explanation: DML refers collectively to inserts, updates and deletes, which were difficult to perform reliably on file-based storage such as HDFS or Amazon S3.

questions.stem: What problem did Apache Spark introduce even though it enabled fast queries and analytics?
options: It could only process batch workloads
It could not read Parquet files
It was not ACID-compliant, risking incomplete writes or corrupted data when jobs failed midway
It required a relational database underneath
It stored all data on a single node
questions.explanation: Spark was not ACID-compliant; without atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability, organisations risked incomplete writes, corrupted data or inconsistencies when jobs failed.

questions.stem: Who originally developed Delta Lake, and what kind of technology is it?
questions.explanation: Delta Lake is an open-source storage layer originally developed by Databricks that extends Spark by adding ACID transactions to big data workloads.

questions.stem: On which file format is Delta Lake built, and in what format is its transaction log stored?
options: Built on CSV, log stored in XML
Built on Apache Parquet, log stored in JSON
Built on Avro, log stored in Parquet
Built on JSON, log stored in CSV
Built on ORC, log stored in YAML
questions.explanation: Delta Lake is built on Apache Parquet, an efficient columnar file format, and introduces a transaction log (the Delta Log) stored in JSON.

questions.stem: What does the Delta Log enable?
options: Transactional guarantees, auditability and rollback by recording every change to the data
Conversion of data into relational tables
questions.explanation: The Delta Log records every change to the data, enabling transactional guarantees, auditability and rollback.

questions.stem: What is the Time Travel feature of Delta Lake?
options: Scheduling jobs to run at a future time
Keeping historical versions of data for rollback or auditing, accessible by timestamp or version number
questions.explanation: Time Travel keeps historical versions of data for rollback or auditing, accessible by timestamp or version number.

questions.stem: How does Delta Lake support Change Data Capture (CDC)?
options: By scanning the whole data set on every run
Through the Delta Log, so downstream systems can consume incremental changes rather than reprocessing entire data sets
By emailing change reports to analysts
By storing changes in a separate relational database
questions.explanation: Through the Delta Log, downstream systems can consume incremental changes rather than reprocessing entire data sets.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the innovations Delta Lake introduced?
questions.explanation: Delta Lake validates incoming data against table definitions while allowing controlled schema changes; unvalidated schema-on-read is the opposite of its schema enforcement.

questions.stem: What broader architecture did Delta Lake lay the groundwork for?
questions.explanation: By transforming data lakes into reliable, production-ready environments, Delta Lake laid the groundwork for the data lakehouse architecture that merges the strengths of warehouses and lakes.
